title: gpuviewer NDJSON contract v1
description: One gpuviewer --json stdout line: a frame or an event. See ndjson-v1.md for semantics. Per the compatibility promise, additive fields may appear in any release, so no object here forbids additional properties; consumers must ignore unknown fields, unknown "type" values, and unknown "kind" values.

ts_ms.description: Unix epoch milliseconds; one timestamp per collection frame.

id.description: Stable device identity (PCI address, or a prefixed key for non-PCI devices).

sample.description: null when the device failed to answer this tick.

util_pct.description: Duty-cycle (time >=1 kernel resident), NOT saturation. Nominally 0-100, but engine-derived sources (Windows WDDM PDH with PDH_FMT_NOCAP100, per-engine busy% summed across pids) can honestly exceed 100 — no maximum is enforced; >100 is real data, not corruption.

util_engine.description: Engine whose busy% util_pct reports when utilization is an engine headline (Windows WDDM busiest engine); null where utilization is device-wide. Open set — never an enum.

encoder_pct.description: Video encoder utilization. Nominally 0-100; engine-derived sources can exceed 100 (see util_pct) — no maximum is enforced.

decoder_pct.description: Video decoder utilization. Nominally 0-100; engine-derived sources can exceed 100 (see util_pct) — no maximum is enforced.

throttle.description: null = this source cannot observe throttling (blind spot, e.g. WDDM counters/macOS) — NOT 'not throttling'; an all-false object is an observed quiet.

other.description: Unknown future driver throttle bits land here, never dropped.

util_pct.description: Per-process GPU utilization. Nominally 0-100; engine-derived sources can exceed 100 (see the sample util_pct description) — no maximum is enforced.

cpu_pct.description: Percent of one core; 100.0 = one full core, can exceed 100 on multithreaded processes.

container.description: Container identity (e.g. docker:1a2b3c4d5e6f); null for host processes or when unknown.

kind.description: All listed kinds are emitted today. Consumers must ignore kinds not in this list (new ones arrive additively per the compatibility promise).

confidence.description: fact = observed state transition; likely = inference, hedged with "likely" in the title.
